# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only feel the available operations; the display, light, and wire contents are unknown to me. I need the Mute to report the manual’s exact rule, and I’ll establish a simple visual code with the Deaf: use 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, and indicate wire numbers with ☝, ✌, or 🤟. I am asking the Deaf to report the visible state using that code, while asking the Mute for the manual instructions.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual's exact defusal procedure. Also interpret Deaf's gestures as follows: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb: display 0; light blue; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, please read the manual and state the exact action to you aloud.

The Deaf has reported the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. I still need the Mute’s manual rule before touching anything, so I am passing these facts to the Mute and asking for the exact action. No action is safe yet.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, light blue, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please state the manual's exact action now.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No manual instruction has reached me, so I cannot safely press the button or cut a wire. I am asking the Mute to provide the rule in a direct, explicit sentence; the Deaf cannot relay spoken content to me, so I will not waste a gesture on that.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="I received no manual instruction. State the exact defusal action explicitly: PUSH, or CUT wire 1, 2, or 3. Do not omit the action.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act yet. I am asking Mute to confirm the manual's required action using a yes-or-no gesture code.

The Deaf is trying to use a yes-or-no gesture code, but gestures cannot convey anything to me. I still need the Mute to speak the manual’s required action directly and unambiguously. I will not touch the bomb yet.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me directly, in words, the exact required action: push the button or cut wire 1, 2, or 3.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute answered no: do not press the button. Hold position and wait for Mute to state the exact manual procedure aloud.

The only confirmed information is that the button must not be pressed. The required wire is still unknown, and the Deaf’s yes/no relay does not identify it. I will ask the Mute to name the wire explicitly rather than infer from the colours.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Which wire must I cut? State exactly: wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible bomb remains display 0, blue light, large button, and wires blue-green-yellow. ? is not an agreed instruction; rely on Mute's spoken manual procedure and do not press anything based on the gesture.

The bomb’s state is unchanged, and no exact wire instruction has reached me. The blue-green-yellow colours are not enough to determine the action without the manual. I will again request a direct spoken wire number from Mute and will take no action.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received the manual procedure. Speak the exact required action to me now: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act on the repeated ? gesture. Ask Mute to state the manual rule and the complete required action aloud, including whether to press the button or cut a specific wire. Act only on that explicit spoken instruction.

The manual’s required action is still not available to me. The Deaf’s gestures cannot communicate the needed instruction, and the bomb must not be touched based on the visible colours alone. I am requesting one final explicit spoken instruction from the Mute, including the exact operation and wire number if applicable.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="State the complete manual rule and required action aloud to me: either press the button, or cut wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3. I will act only on that explicit instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb is unchanged. Ask Mute for the manual's exact procedure aloud; do not act on any gesture. Mute is being asked whether the required action involves cutting a wire rather than pressing the button.

The manual instruction still has not reached me. Since the Mute is being asked to distinguish cutting from pressing, I will request the exact wire number as soon as that is known and continue waiting without touching the bomb.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer aloud with the complete action now: PRESS, or CUT 1, CUT 2, or CUT 3. Do not answer only yes or no.")
wait()
```
